_comment: Tier-2: strategy.Check() called before strategy.Initialize() SEGFAULTS on a SlidingCableElement3D3N model — the element Check dereferences the constitutive-law pointer, which is only cloned in Initialize(). Pitfall (kratos.cable_net #0). Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). REPRODUCED: a child process builds the strategy, prints REACHED_STRATEGY, then dies on strat.Check() with returncode -11 (SIGSEGV) and no Kratos exception and no Python traceback. The documented fix is asserted too — calling strat.Initialize() first and THEN Check() exits 0 and prints SURVIVED — so the fixture pins a crash that has a remedy rather than a crash alone. Run in a subprocess because a SIGSEGV cannot be caught in-process; the returncode is the observation. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass.
